llm.summary: The skill is coherent for Alibaba Cloud SLS alert work, but needs review because it includes an unverified remote shell installer and can change live alerting and notification configuration.

dimensions.detail: Aliyun CLI, network access, configured cloud credentials, contact data, webhook destinations, and SLS mutation permissions are proportionate to managing alerts, but they are sensitive and should be limited to the requested account/project/resource scope.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill package has no install hook, but its prerequisite guide tells macOS/Linux users to execute a mutable remote Aliyun CLI installer directly with Bash without pinning or checksum/signature verification.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are scoped to user-requested SLS operations, preserve unrelated fields, use dry runs/readbacks for writes, avoid credential dumping, and use configured CLI profiles; destructive operations are documented but not hidden.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No background agents, memory writes, services, or hidden persistence were found; persistent cloud resources and local CLI/plugin installation are expected parts of the workflow, with the remote installer risk covered separately.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose matches the artifact: SKILL.md routes users through alert rule management, notification resource management, and event diagnosis, with bundled offline validators for alert and ResourceRecord JSON.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable giving the agent access to your Aliyun CLI context for SLS alerting. Avoid the curl-to-bash installer path unless you independently trust and verify the Aliyun CLI installer, use least-privilege RAM permissions, confirm every create/update/delete against the intended project or resource namespace, and treat notification users, webhooks, headers, and dynamic callback URLs as sensitive.
llm.findings:
[T03] unexpected: Installing Aliyun CLI is purpose-related, but the documented curl-to-bash installer is an unsafe under-verified prerequisite path; it is user-visible rather than hidden, so this supports Review rather than malicious classification.
[TP4] expected: The scanner's capability-mismatch concern is downgraded: the artifact is not only offline validators, because SKILL.md and references document SLS alert rule, notification resource, and diagnosis workflows.
[LP3] expected: The skill lacks a separate tool-permission manifest, but the instructions do scope work to Aliyun SLS CLI/API operations, configured profiles, least-privilege RAM guidance, and credential non-disclosure.
[EA2] expected: The cited text is a protective instruction not to ask for or expose credentials, not evidence of autonomous destructive behavior.
[SQP-2] expected: Dynamic callbacks, webhook integrations, and delete/update operations are expected for alerting; the docs include some warnings about shared resources and secrets, though users should still review external callback and deletion impact carefully.
[SQP-1] expected: The labels/annotations activation language is broad, but it stays within the alert-rule workflow and does not introduce unrelated authority.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese-locale documentation links and documented locale values appear tied to Alibaba Cloud SLS references and service examples, not to hidden behavior or forced agent output language.
